acceptance: A unit test on DataFusion covering ungrouped `select` of `var`, `quantile`, `std`, and their `filter(...)` forms returns the same values as Polars on the same data, and fails on current develop.
Existing DataFusion select tests for plain projections still pass (no projection is routed to `aggregate`).
PR merged; its body lists every aggregate terminal checked and the detection approach chosen.
description:
## Problem
`UnifiedLazyFrame.select` on DataFusion sends an expression to `DataFrame.aggregate([], ...)` only when its text contains a pattern in `_DATAFUSION_AGGREGATE_PATTERNS` (`benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py`): sum, avg, count, min, max, first_value, last_value, stddev, approx_distinct. `var` renders as `var(x)` and `quantile` as `approx_percentile_cont(...)`, so both go to `DataFrame.select` and DataFusion 55.0.0 fails with `This feature is not implemented: Physical plan does not support logical expression AggregateFunction(...)`. The filtered forms (`expr.filter(cond).var()` / `.quantile()`, which wrap the value in CASE) fail the same way. Grouped `agg` is unaffected.

## Evidence (2026-11-17, datafusion 55.0.0)
`df.select(f.var_samp(col("x")))` fails; `df.aggregate([], [f.var_samp(col("x"))])` returns 1.6667. Same for `approx_percentile_cont` (aggregate returns 2.5) and for the CASE-wrapped filtered variance.

## Change
Make aggregate detection in `select` cover every aggregate terminal `UnifiedExpr` can produce on DataFusion, including var and quantile, aliased and filtered forms. Prefer detecting the expression's variant (AggregateFunction anywhere in the tree) over extending the text pattern list; if the variant walk is not available through the Python API, extend the patterns and say why in the PR.

## Decision gate
If a select mixes aggregate and non-aggregate expressions, keep today's behaviour (whatever it is) and record it; do not widen scope to new semantics.

## Guardrails
No platform-name branches in benchmark query code; no reference-answer, fixture or SQL changes. One PR.
